title: Main-sequence dust dimmers are not metal-rich: Gaia XP metallicities of 76 dimmers against matched field stars reject the beta = 2 giant-planet law that hot-Jupiter hosts follow in the same test
abstract: Question: Many proposed sources of the dust that makes main-sequence stars dim deeply and aperiodically need giant planets. Giant-planet occurrence increases as 10^(beta [Fe/H]) with beta about 1.2-2.0, so such sources predict metal-rich dimmers. Nobody tested this. Approach: We compared the SHBoost 2024 Gaia XP metallicity of 76 dust dimmers (66 ZTF main-sequence dippers of Tzanidakis et al. 2025 and 10 campaign field-dwarf dimmers, including Gaia20cdd) with a median of 162 controls per dimmer in the same sky field and with the same G, BP-RP and parallax. A conditional likelihood over the matched sets gives beta. 3,013 LAMOST DR11 dwarfs in the same fields calibrate SHBoost (slope 1.12, 95 percent 1.08-1.16, near 1.1 down to G = 17-18.5). Planet hosts in the same test are positive and negative controls. Results: The mean dimmer offset from the controls is -0.031 dex (95 percent -0.062 to -0.002), or -0.005 dex (-0.037 to +0.025) after removal of the extinction-metallicity degeneracy; beta = 2 predicts +0.091 dex. Thus beta = -0.06 (-0.70 to +0.58) with this correction and -0.60 (-1.22 to +0.02) without it; beta = 2 has p < 1e-9 and beta = 1 has p = 0.001. All subsets of 33 or more dimmers reject beta = 2. The same test gives beta = 2.22 (1.60-2.86) for 65 hot-Jupiter hosts, 1.68 (0.92-2.44) for 43 hot-Jupiter hosts with G >= 14.5, and 0.40 (-0.16 to 0.98) for 64 Kepler small-planet hosts. Dimmers also have higher SHBoost extinction than their controls (median +0.07 mag, mean rank 0.68 against 0.45 for planet hosts, p = 6e-9), also when they were quiet during Gaia DR3; this agrees with time-averaged circumstellar extinction. Conclusion: In this sample, dust dimmers have field-star metallicity (beta <= 0.6), so models in which most dimming dust comes from systems with giant planets are unlikely. Limitations: SHBoost is a machine-learning estimate partly trained on LAMOST-based labels; a treatment of the quoted errors as pure noise widens the limit to beta < 3.0, but LAMOST and the hot-Jupiter control reject that error model; 17 of 93 dimmers lack values; the A_V excess may come from the TZ25 selection; only one dimmer has a LAMOST spectrum. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-330c7ea895e4, topic astronomy, machine dell, model Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5).

display.caption: (a) Mean SHBoost [M/H] offset of dust dimmers and planet hosts from matched same-field controls, with 95 percent bootstrap intervals. Black marks: offsets expected for a selection 10^(beta [Fe/H]) with beta = 1 (bar) and beta = 2 (diamond). Dimmers show no positive offset; hot-Jupiter hosts show the expected one. (b) Offsets of individual stars against Gaia G.

Profile likelihood of beta in P ~ 10^(beta [M/H]) for each sample against its matched controls. Dimmers (red; dash-dot: A_V-corrected) give beta near 0; hot-Jupiter hosts give beta near 2 also at G >= 14.5; small-planet hosts give a weak dependence. Dashed: error model that treats quoted SHBoost errors as pure noise, which the LAMOST calibration rejects. Shaded: published giant-planet values.

(a) Calibration: LAMOST DR11 [Fe/H] against SHBoost [M/H] for 3,013 dwarfs in the dimmer fields, binned by G; the relation stays near slope 1.1 at faint G. (b) Mean rank among matched controls for nine parameters; dimmers have high SHBoost A_V ranks, planet hosts do not.
